more.question: N5
more.good_when: Every kind of row the colleague from accounting may save has a test named for it, so a maintainer whose test fails knows which kind broke: a row with more than three fields, such as a description that holds a semicolon, is refused with its row number just as a row of two fields is; a quantity written in digits other than 0 to 9 is refused; a price of Infinity is refused as NaN is; and a negative price, as on a credit line, is either taken or refused, with a test that says which.

more.question: N7
more.good_when: Every way the invoice could come out wrong fails a test. Today the tests still pass when the tax is rounded half to even instead of half up (210.50 at 19% gives 40.00 either way), when only rows of fewer than three fields are refused, so a row of four fields stops the command with a Python trace instead of a message naming the row, and when a quantity in digits other than 0 to 9 is taken. Once it's good, a cent that rounds differently under half up than under half even, a row of four fields, and such a quantity each fail a test when broken, and each line of invoicer either serves a case that a test runs or is gone: today no test runs the total of invoicer.totals or how a Line shows itself, so either could break unseen.
